label: copy-phase input s (fed back from original position >= 1)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the token fed back as input is s, at steps with recall_idx >= 2, i.e. the s being copied came from original position 1 or later. It never fires during the original phase or on <DEL>, never on other input tokens, and almost never at recall_idx 1, when s is the first token copied back. Every copy-phase s input at recall_idx >= 2 activates it (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude is larger when the s sits later in the sequence: the top examples (~0.96-1.0 of max) have s at original position 6-7, and the lowest-quartile examples have s at position 1-4. Which token is being output, neighbouring tokens, and L have little effect beyond that.

issues: The test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.990, F1 0.995, mass recall 0.9997, correlation 0.99. The predicate has no false positives on the test split.

Every one of the 759 missed test activations is an s copied back at recall_idx 1 (s at original position 0), with activations of only 0.01-0.03 of max, and together they hold 0.0% of the activation mass. So the claim that it 'almost never fires at recall_idx 1' holds in effect: it does fire at small values on 756 dev steps, but those are negligible.
The phase claims check out. On the dev split there are 0 activations in the original phase and 0 on <DEL>. Activations on input tokens other than s are about 22 steps out of 75k.

The magnitude claim holds: the top examples have s at original position 6-7 (0.96-1.0 of max) and the lowest-quartile examples have s early. One small overclaim: the explanation says neighbouring tokens have little effect, but an s fed back right after another s is weaker (about 0.80-0.85 in the top examples where the first s is about 0.97-0.99, and 0.56 vs 0.82 in a low example). This affects magnitude only, not whether the feature fires.
